t: Report On Two Chinese Deportees From Japan Named Zung Dao Kwei And Zung Dao Tsing

pages.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
JAN MUNICIPAL POLICE
File No. REGISTRY
D
S. 2, Special Branch Station,
REPORT
Date. January 10th 1935.
Subject: arrival in Shanghai of Sung Dao Wei (陳道桂) and Sung Dao Tsing
(陳道進), Chinese deportees from Japan.
Made by ... Forwarded by. J.B.Ross

According to information received by the local Japanese
Consular Police from the State Police (Northern Japan), the
undermentioned two Chinese were deported from Japan as
undesirable characters by the S.S. "Aso Maru" which arrived
in Shanghai on December 29, 1934.

(1) Sung Dao Wei, 47, cloth pedlar by occupation, native
of Fukien, residing in Morioka Cho, Morioka, arrived in Japan
in May, 1923. During his stay in Asahikawa, Hokkaido, in
March, 1933, he received a quantity of blue serge, stolen by
a Chinese named Sung Chun Chu (陳君举), residing in Sapporo,
and disposed of the same article in May, 1933, to Sung Tsun Ching
(陳觀鏡), Chinese, and I. Fujita, Japanese, both living in
Morioka. During the period from 1926 to 1933, he procured
on behalf of Too Tui Yuan (杜德源), No. 5, 2 Chome, Ichijo
Dori, Asahikawa, on more than 50 occasions a large quantity of
opium from Foh Zung (福順), a Chinese firm, in Kyoto.

(2) Sung Dao Tsing, 35, cloth pedlar, native of Fukien,
residing in Moriukata Cho, Morioka, was sentenced to a fine of
Yen 10 for gambling by the Morioka Court in 1927. Between June,
1929 and December, 1930 he obtained on credit piece-goods to
the amount of Yen 161.87 from the Akazawa Drapery Store, in
Morioka, and Yen 400 worth of piece-goods from Teikichi Ohta,
Japanese, in Kyoto. In January, 1931 he absconded to China
and revisited Japan in November, 1934. Payment of these
accounts has not yet been made.

Their destination in Shanghai is given to the shipping
company as c/o Foh Sing Co. (福新公司), No. 31 Dong Tsung Li
(同春里), Kungping Road. This firm is, in fact, a boarding
house used by Fukienese who are proceeding to and returning from

报告
日期：1935年1月10日。
事由：自日本被驱逐出境的华人陈道桂（Sung Dao Wei）和陈道进（Sung Dao Tsing）抵达上海。
制作人…… 转交人：J.B.Ross

据当地日本领事警察从国家警察（日本北部）收到的情报，下述两名华人因被视为不受欢迎分子，由“阿苏丸”号（S.S. "Aso Maru"）轮船从日本驱逐出境，该轮于1934年12月29日抵达上海。

(1) 陈道桂（Sung Dao Wei），47岁，职业为布贩，福建籍，居住于盛冈市盛冈町，于1923年5月抵达日本。1933年3月，他在北海道旭川停留期间，接收了一批由居住在札幌的华人陈君举（Sung Chun Chu）盗窃的蓝色哔叽呢，并于1933年5月将该批货物出售给同样居住在盛冈的华人陈观镜（Sung Tsun Ching）和日本人I. Fujita。在1926年至1933年期间，他代表居住在旭川一条通二丁目5号的杜德源（Too Tui Yuan），先后50多次从京都的一家华商字号福顺（Foh Zung）处获取大量鸦片。

(2) 陈道进（Sung Dao Tsing），35岁，布贩，福建籍，居住于盛冈市盛冈片町（Moriukata Cho），曾于1927年被盛冈法院以赌博罪判处10日元罚款。在1929年6月至1930年12月期间，他从盛冈的赤泽绸缎店（Akazawa Drapery Store）赊购了价值161.87日元的匹头货物，并从京都的日本人太田帝吉（Teikichi Ohta）处赊购了价值400日元的匹头货物。1931年1月他潜逃至中国，并于1934年11月再次前往日本。上述账款至今未付。

他们向船公司申报的在上海目的地为：公平路同春里31号福新公司（Foh Sing Co.）转交。该公司实际上是一家供往返于
